notAssessed: In JavaScript and TypeScript, data flow is followed across functions and modules when a resolved call hands caller data from a request handler to another function, up to four calls deep, through ESM and CommonJS imports, re-exports, tsconfig paths and class methods, including the fields of an object argument. zod, yup, joi and valibot schemas are read field by field. A function handed caller data from more than two other modules is treated as a shared utility and not followed into. Values that travel through event emitters, queues, stored callbacks, dynamic dispatch or a call the engine cannot resolve are not connected.

JavaScript, TypeScript and Python source is parsed. Other languages, configuration files, and infrastructure definitions are not analysed, and templates are read only where a Python view renders them.
Runtime behaviour, authentication state, and business rules are not exercised by the static pass; dynamic validation is the host agent's part of the assessment.

Dependency findings compare installed versions (from the lockfile, or exact pins in package.json without one) against an offline advisory snapshot. A finding is raised only where application code imports and uses an export the advisory names; a vulnerable package reached only through another package is listed as present but not reached, because this scan does not follow calls inside dependencies.

A route is reported as the file declares it, or as another module in this scan registered the handler under. Where a router is itself mounted under a prefix further up the application, that prefix is not part of the reported path.
4 handler(s) were attributed to a route declared in a different module. The route is reported as that router spells it, without any prefix the router is mounted under.

No entry point was recognised in 2 of 3 parsed file(s). Data-flow checks need an entry point to know which values a caller controls, so in those files they did not run — treat a clean result for this project as unproven rather than as evidence of safety.

POST /api/import fetched a destination supplied entirely by the caller and returned HTTP 200. No allowlist was consulted, so the destination is the caller's choice.

Python entry points are recognised for FastAPI and Flask. Django, class-based views (Flask MethodView), plain Starlette, aiohttp, Tornado and other frameworks are parsed, but their handlers are not recognised as entry points, so data-flow checks do not start from them.

Python data flow follows calls into functions and methods defined in this project, across modules, including functions handed to a background task, thread or task queue with their arguments. A value one route stores in the session is followed, by key, to the routes that read it back, and a value a route writes to a stored record's field is followed, by field name, to unescaped markup and template source that read the field back. It does not follow other callbacks, dynamic dispatch, values kept in caches, stored data reaching other sinks, or decorators that rewrite a handler's arguments.
Python dependency manifests (requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, poetry.lock) are not compared against advisories.
